chapter: Joining Raeburn and work for other leaders
title: Betty Hutton, Hollywood and leaving Raeburn
summary: He went to Hollywood for Betty Hutton, who left him within weeks, and stayed in Los Angeles.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Did you decide you wanted to be a songwriter or just found yourself being a songwriter?
It was convenient at the time to become a songwriter. I fancied myself in love with Betty Hutton.
Did she record any of your material?
No, but I wrote some stuff for her, which is in the Paramount archives. They'll probably lay there until the end of time. But no, she never did the stuff.

I came out to Hollywood, we embraced we went back to her place, we went to bed together, professed undying love for each other and in the morning I took her to the plane where she was going on a USO tour and I said goodby sweetheart and she said okay, it will only be six weeks and when I get back we'll be married immediately. I said okay, darling, have a good trip and I'll see you at the altar; that was the last time I saw her, when I put her on the plane.
That was a fast love affair anyway.
That brought me out to the coast and that had me leave Raeburn.
That was 1945 or so, I guess?

Right. That was '45. I never saw her again but about six weeks later I got a call from the head of the studio, who said Betty felt pretty badly about things but she couldn't bring herself to come back on the lot and face me, so would I please leave so that their star could come back to the lot in comfort. And without her, in those days, Paramount was up a creek. She was bringing in all the money, she was their big star. That was it, she had a change of heart and couldn't face me. That took me away from Paramount and put me into town where after a few months--
Hal McKusick was living with me at the time--
By into town, you mean back in L.A.?
L.A., I was living in L.A. and I decided to stay there.
